Subject: Request: clarify availability credits + maintenance carveout in Performance Annex

Hiro/Laura —

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. Procurement asked me to surface a couple of outstanding items before we can route the order form through our legal team:

1) Availability credit calculation: we need the explicit formula used to compute monthly service credits (per-incident vs aggregated monthly uptime). Current draft references "service credits" without the math. Can you add an illustrative example and the exact percent thresholds?

2) Scheduled maintenance carveout: our internal ops needs a definitive window for scheduled maintenance (max weekly minutes, notification SLA, and a hard cap per quarter). Right now the annex says "scheduled maintenance as mutually agreed" which is too vague for our auditors.

3) Evidence packages: our security team will request SOC2 evidence + monthly uptime reports for the first 6 months. Is that deliverable from Redwood or do you expect self-service access only?

We've attached the order form draft with margin notes. Please send a proposed redline for the Performance Annex and explicit wording we can show legal. We have a soft procurement deadline of EOD Thu 12 Feb.

Best,
Amanda
Sr. Procurement Manager
MedAlign Health

Subject: Re: Request: clarify availability credits + maintenance carveout in Performance Annex

Amanda —

Thanks for the clear list. Drafting answers inline and attaching a redline for the Performance Annex (Performance_Annex_v3_redline.pdf). High level:

- Availability credits: we calculate credits on the per-calendar-month aggregated availability percentage across the customer account. Example wording and two worked examples are in the redline (see section 2.1). In short, credits are a percentage of monthly fees, applied after the first 99.5% availability threshold; the schedule tiers are 99.0-99.5 => 5% credit, 98.0-98.99 => 15% credit, <98.0 => 30% credit. We can tweak tiers for enterprise commitments but need to align on monitoring signal.

- Scheduled maintenance carveout: proposed explicit clause: "Scheduled maintenance windows shall not exceed 240 minutes per calendar month without prior written agreement; Redwood will provide >=72 hours advance notice for non-emergency maintenance and <=30 minutes for emergency maintenance where feasible. Quarterly non-emergency maintenance shall not exceed 720 minutes total." That language and notification SLAs are in the redline.

- Evidence packages: we can provide SOC 2 Type II report and monthly uptime reports for the first 6 months. For production telemetry we will grant an operations dashboard view and can export CSVs on request. If MedAlign requires continuous streaming of uptime telemetry to a third-party, we should scope that as an add-on.

I cc'd Monica from our procurement operations to advise on procurement steps and DocuSign path.

I'll hold for your feedback; if these clauses look acceptable we can circulate a clean order form for signature.

Thanks,
Hiro
Sr. Product Manager, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Thanks — the redline looks good overall. A couple of quick items from legal/procurement review:

• Credit schedule: legal prefers a per-incident credit path (we escalate credits per incident severity) rather than aggregated monthly. Would Redwood accept a hybrid: per-incident credits up to a monthly cap, with the aggregated monthly fallback? We attached a markup in the Word draft.

• Notification: 72-hour notice for non-emergency maintenance is fine; can you add a requirement to post maintenance windows to a status page and include a reference ID for each maintenance event in uptime reports?

• Evidence access: please send the SOC2 link and a sample monthly report by EOD Thu (we need to attach to our audit packet).

If we can get these three items final, I can turn the package over to legal for a fast sign-off. PO will come separately.

Amanda
